assessments.reasoning: Printed I-16 §3.2.8 describes an additive defined-value component and a descendant-pointer component. For a qualifying existing named reference, both the no-subscript and prefix cases expressly admit a matching descendant that existed and was killed. Section 3.6.10 on I-37 confirms that killing a descendant while leaving its ancestor intact does not change the ancestor’s $DATA result.

challenge.method: Compare a defined value alone, a descendant with no target value, both components, no applicable descendant, an unmatched sibling, killing only the last descendant, and killing the target itself. Compare the exact printed historical witness with the current YottaDB function-status table.
challenge.results: The historical digit separates target value from descendant information. A corresponding previously killed descendant may contribute to the latter for an existing unchanged ancestor. A sibling with a different prefix does not. Killing the target follows the separate zero-state provision in §3.6.10. The YottaDB manual describes whether a node currently has descendants and supplies no basis for exporting the historical retained-pointer rule to that implementation.

limitations: The historical nonzero pointer case requires the named variable to exist and the descendant to match the named branch. An untouched ancestor is distinct from a killed target. The result does not expose a physical pointer or certify later implementations.
